title: Must every height be measured again without the shoes?
description: Leeza measures the heights of all twenty four students and finds an average of one hundred and fifty point two centimetres, but the uniform shoes add one centimetre to every height. The video uses the idea that shifting every value shifts the mean to correct the average without measuring again.
teaching_notes: One idea: when every value is too big by the same amount, the mean is too big by that amount, so subtract it from the mean. Watch for students who share the one centimetre among twenty four students, instead of taking one centimetre from every height.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 3)
video_script.why: The child could measure all twenty four heights again, but a simpler way uses what happens to the mean when every value shifts by the same amount.
video_script.substitution: Treat the shoes as the same one centimetre added to every height, and take that one centimetre off the average.
video_script.anchor: a row of twenty four students standing in uniform shoes, with the average height 150.2 centimetres written above
video_script.payoff_line: The correct average height is one hundred and forty nine point two centimetres

final_answer.value: No need to measure again; the correct average is 149.2 cm
final_answer.spoken: there is no need to measure again, and the correct average is one hundred and forty nine point two centimetres
